key_insight: qReduMIS uses QAOA measurements to identify frozen nodes that shrink the graph before classical optimization, enabling practical quantum-assisted portfolio selection on real market data.
engineering_relevance: The pipeline shows how near-term quantum hardware can contribute as a preprocessing accelerator inside a hybrid optimization workflow rather than needing to solve the full problem end to end.
method: Build a market correlation graph and map portfolio selection to a Maximum Independent Set problem.
Run QAOA on reduced graph kernels to sample independent sets and detect frozen vertices.
Apply provably optimal classical reductions recursively, then solve the remaining smaller instance.
evidence_signal: Validated on four major indices up to 225 assets and on Quantinuum trapped-ion hardware, qReduMIS achieved average approximation ratios of at least 0.96, with success probabilities of 0.40 for S&P 100 and 0.95 for Nikkei 225, and improved time-to-solution scaling on 73 graphs in emulator tests.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of QAOA samples and graph reductions, so hardware noise or weak sampling on larger kernels could reduce the frozen-node identification benefit.
paper_title: Quantum-Informed Portfolio Selection: An End-to-End Pipeline Validated on Trapped-Ion Hardware with Real Market Data
